strengths: The problem has a clear audience in machine learning for code, software analysis, and security. Transferring supervision from source code and generated descriptions into an LLVM representation is a useful research direction.
The frozen source/comment encoder and learned interpolation provide an understandable framework. Figures 2–4 and Algorithm 1 communicate the overall training pipeline reasonably well.

The evaluation covers four discriminative and generative tasks and includes component ablations. Reported results are encouraging: function-name accuracy reaches 33.41 versus 29.41 for RoBERTa, and summarization BLEU reaches 34.36 versus 32.43 for GraphCodeBERT.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 evaluation protocol. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify disjoint sets of 64 training, 16 development, and 24 test labels, while Section 4.2 describes supervised classification into 104 classes. Ordinary supervised classification does not explain evaluation on labels absent from training. If this is actually retrieval or similarity evaluation, specify the training objective, query/candidate sets, ranking procedure, and metric definitions. This ambiguity affects both the main results and every reported ablation.

Necessary: Align the binary-analysis claims with the actual inputs. The experiments use LLVM IR produced during source compilation, rather than representations recovered from stripped executables. Figures 7–8 retain informative function, type, and global names. Such IR is not trivially interchangeable with stripped machine code, as the opening footnote suggests. Either evaluate an executable-to-representation pipeline appropriate to the stated application or narrow the claims to compiler-generated LLVM IR under the documented symbol-retention conditions.

Necessary: Separate interpolation benefits from additional training. CONTRABIN-PCL receives 10 pretraining epochs, whereas the full models receive 30 or 70. The interpolation ablation therefore changes both the method and training budget. Section 4.5 asserts convergence without supporting learning curves. Matched training-budget controls are needed to attribute improvements to interpolation. The current ablations also do not establish the separate benefits of scalar interpolation, feature-wise interpolation, and their staged ordering; narrow those component claims or isolate these effects.

Necessary: Make evaluation independence verifiable. Section 3.2 describes using a pretraining holdout for downstream AnghaBench tasks, but reports generation performance on a validation set while reserving the test set for embedding visualization. The manuscript does not adequately specify pretraining split sizes, model-selection use of validation data, or safeguards against duplicate and repository overlap across splits. Document the complete split construction and establish that the reported evaluation data were held out from training and model selection.

Necessary: Support or narrow the semantic-comprehension claims. CodeT5-generated comments are the only documented summary targets, so overlap scores primarily establish agreement with synthetic descriptions. BLEU, GLEU, exact match, and two examples do not establish that reconstructed programs preserve behavior or that summaries help humans. Add independent semantic assessment of summaries and functional checks of generated code, or restrict conclusions to reference-text prediction. RQ2 explicitly mentions human perception, but no corresponding assessment is presented.

Necessary: Specify the implemented model and objective sufficiently for reproduction. Encoder identities and initialization, tokenization, projection details, and the decoder used for generation are insufficiently documented. Equation 4 omits the softmax described in the preceding text, leaving raw similarities as cross-entropy targets. Clarify normalization, target construction, gradient flow through targets, and modality sampling. Definitions and implementations of MAP, MAR, MAF1, and the inconsistently named GLUE/GLEU metric are also needed.

Necessary: Correct unsupported interpretations of the evidence. Section 4.1 incorrectly reasons that unique programs should not cluster and that fewer t-SNE clusters prove better representations; neither conclusion follows from the visualization. Treat these plots as illustrations or provide quantitative evidence in the original embedding space. Performance claims also need calibration: in Table 6, CONTRABIN has lower BLEU than GraphCodeBERT and improves exact match by only 0.43 percentage points, with no uncertainty estimates. These results do not establish uniformly substantial or robust superiority.

Optional: Enlarge the code examples and figure labels, streamline the repeated human-learning analogies, and improve cross-references and terminology consistency. Broader compiler and architecture experiments would be useful extensions if the paper is first scoped accurately. The rejection is based on substantive gaps in claim support and experimental specification, rather than a requirement for greater novelty or state-of-the-art performance.
